market_context.summary: Supply-shock inflation with a hawkish Fed leaning into it — not a growth scare and not a disinflation glide. August CPI ran 3.4% YoY with core +0.3% m/m, driven by the oil supply shock that followed the late-February Strait of Hormuz disruption, and Kalshi prices a 25bp HIKE on Wednesday 2026-09-16 at 79c with a further hike priced for December at 59c. The curve confirms it: the 2-year at 4.56% sits ~93bp ABOVE effective fed funds at 3.63%, so the front end is pricing tightening, not easing. The dispersion is the tradeable fact — fossil energy is the only leadership on the board (XLE within 1.6% of its 150-day high) while every bond proxy sits at or near its 150-day low (TLT +0.25% off, XLU +1.3% off) and housing has broken with the 30-year mortgage through 7.07%. Today is a Sunday: equity levels are Friday 2026-09-11 closes and all equity entries are for the Monday 2026-09-14 open.

catalyst.event: Nymex 3:2:1 crack spread near $69.92/bbl against a $21.68 ten-year average, plus a planned separation of the Lubricants & Specialties segment into an independent public company over the next 12-18 months
catalyst.action: buy at market on the next open (Mon 2026-09-14) inside 105.50-109.50; add only above the 112.165 400-day high. RED TEAM: stop widened from 99.00 to 97.75.

recommendations.thesis: HF Sinclair earns the crack spread rather than the crude price, and that spread is at an extreme: the Nymex 3:2:1 sits near $69.92/bbl against a $21.68 average for the decade to Feb 2026. The 8-K shows it converting - Q2 2026 adjusted refinery gross margin of $25.95 per produced barrel sold versus $16.50 a year earlier, and net income of $892 million or $4.93 per diluted share against $208 million or $1.10. Separately and independently of the spread, management is separating the Lubricants & Specialties segment into a listed company over 12-18 months, which is a structural value-unlock that does not depend on crude staying where it is.
recommendations.key_risk: This is peak-cycle earnings and the multiple lies about it. $4.93 of quarterly EPS annualises to roughly 5.5x at 107.84, which looks cheap and is the classic refiner value trap - a low P/E on a cyclical top is a warning, not a bargain, because the denominator is about to fall. Crack spreads are the most violently mean-reverting number in energy and this one is three times its ten-year average purely because Hormuz transit is impaired; a ceasefire re-rates DINO down 30% in days through any sane stop. RED TEAM ADDED, and it is the risk this idea omitted while its two lane-mates named it: the Fed hikes on 2026-09-16 explicitly to destroy the demand side of this same energy shock, and refined-product demand is what the crack spread is levered to - so the week's dominant event works against this position, not for it. This report also holds DVN in the same lane; one ceasefire headline takes both through their stops together.
recommendations.counter_argument: CNBC ran the bear case explicitly on 2026-08-17: refiner stocks are on a nearly unprecedented run and history says it ends soon. DINO is +88% over six months and +22.6% in the last month, and the last three refining cycles all ended with the spread collapsing faster than the equity did.

evidence.detail: Read the Q2 2026 8-K. Exact figures: adjusted refinery gross margin $25.95 per produced barrel sold vs $16.50 in Q2 2025 (+57%); net income attributable to stockholders $892 million, or $4.93 per diluted share, vs $208 million or $1.10 a year earlier (+329%). The company plans to separate its Lubricants & Specialties segment through the capital markets into an independent, publicly traded company over the next 12-18 months, and will retire its Mississauga, Ontario base oil refining assets by 2027 while keeping regional blending via new sourcing agreements.

Open-market insider buying: 3 purchases by 2 distinct buyers totalling $2.42M over six months, net +$705K against sales. Franklin Myers bought 15,000 shares at $69.11 on 2026-05-18 and another 15,000 at $85.30 on 2026-08-11 - a repeat purchase after the run was well advanced. Relative strength: DINO +22.64% 1m vs XLE +6.73% and SPY -1.06%; +88.24% 6m vs XLE +13.27%.

112.165 is the 400-day high, printed intraday on 2026-09-11 before closing 107.84, so it is a tested level rather than a round number. Support shelf 103.12-104.81 from the Sept 2-4 lows sits above a rising SMA20 at 100.294; SMA50 91.285 and SMA200 66.721 are far beneath. ATR14 3.897, so the 99.00 stop is 2.18 ATR from entry. Avg dollar volume $273M/day.

RED TEAM: this item is only partly independent of the positioning item above - its first half restates the same Franklin Myers purchase (15,000sh @ 85.30, 2026-08-11) already counted there, which is why conviction came down from 5 to 4. What is genuinely additional: the sell side is not crowded - analyst bullish share is only 52.2% (4 strong buy, 8 buy, 9 hold, 1 sell, 1 strong sell) and has FALLEN 2.3 points over four months, so the CNBC mean-reversion case is not yet consensus positioning. The Lubricants separation also gives a value path that survives a spread normalisation, which the pure mean-reversion case does not account for.

catalyst.event: A post-patent-cliff re-rating: Pfizer trades at 10x forward earnings against Bristol Myers at 11x and Merck at 18x, while the $10B Metsera acquisition builds a clinical-stage obesity portfolio into a market projected at $150B
catalyst.action: accumulate in thirds below 27.85; add the second third under 26.50 and the last only under 25.50 if the cliff narrative sells it off. No need to rush - this is a multi-quarter build, not a trade

recommendations.thesis: Pfizer is a quality business de-rated on a real but finite problem, which is the shape this report should own more of. The market prices the loss-of-exclusivity cliff - $17-20B of annual revenue to generics between 2026 and 2030 - and prices almost nothing for what replaces it: five regulatory decisions, eight key readouts and 19 pivotal study starts in 2026, plus a Metsera-derived incretin and amylin portfolio whose lead GLP-1 showed 16% mean weight loss in Phase 2b. At 10x forward against BMY at 11x and MRK at 18x, a re-rate to 12.6x is the whole idea, and a 7% dividend pays to wait.
recommendations.key_risk: The invalidation is specific and is not a price: the Metsera-derived incretin/amylin assets failing to advance to Phase 3, or reading out materially below the 16% Phase 2b weight-loss benchmark, would remove the only thing large enough to offset the cliff - and a dividend cut would be the confirming signal that the cliff is overwhelming cash flow. Either of those, and 25 is the target rather than the floor. Note also that at 27.72 PFE already sits AT the $28 median analyst target, so the crowd sees no upside from here.
recommendations.counter_argument: RBC Capital initiated at Underperform with a $25 target and called the $15-20B revenue cliff through 2030 insurmountable with limited near-term pipeline visibility. That is the bear case in one line and it is not obviously wrong - big pharma has repeatedly failed to replace expiring blockbusters on schedule, and COVID revenue is still shrinking, to roughly $5B in 2026 from $6.7B in 2025.

evidence.detail: Three distinct insiders bought $2.83M in the open market in August 2026, and all three are now in profit rather than underwater: CEO Albert Bourla 38,000sh @ $26.34 (2026-08-12), director Mortimer Buckley 37,632sh @ $25.52 and director Ronald Blaylock 39,231sh @ $25.46 (both 2026-08-05), against a 27.72 close. Relative strength confirms: PFE +5.36% 1m vs XLV -1.83% and SPY -1.06%. Sell-side is NOT crowded at 38.9% bullish and falling.

PFE trades at 10x forward earnings vs Bristol Myers Squibb at 11x and Merck at 18x. The 35.00 target is a re-rate to roughly 12.6x forward - inside the peer range and still well below Merck - not a new multiple regime. Cross-check: the 28-analyst range is $25-$36, so 35 sits near the top of what the street already models rather than outside it, and the bear anchor of 25 is the bottom of that same range.

Against RBC insurmountable-cliff call: Pfizer spent $10B on Metsera specifically to buy a clinical-stage obesity portfolio with monthly-dosed incretin and amylin candidates, and the lead GLP-1 delivered 16% mean weight loss in Phase 2b - a real asset in a market projected at $150B, not a promise. The market is pricing the cliff at 10x while a peer with a comparable cliff (BMY) holds 11x and the sector leader holds 18x.

catalyst.event: FDA PDUFA target action date of 2026-11-22 for MOLBREEVI (molgramostim inhalation solution) in autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis, under Priority Review
catalyst.action: UPDATE TO AN EXISTING POSITION - HOLD the long opened 2026-08-23 at 5.35, stop unchanged at 4.60. Entry zone stays open for anyone not yet filled. Plan to trim into the run-up rather than hold the full position through a binary decision

recommendations.thesis: UPDATE TO EXISTING POSITION - HOLD, thesis intact and the catalyst is now dated. Savara has a PDUFA action date of 2026-11-22 for molgramostim in autoimmune PAP, an orphan indication with no approved therapy. The three-month delay from the original 2026-08-22 date is the thing to understand correctly: the FDA extended it because Savara own responses to information requests counted as a major amendment, and the Agency explicitly did not cite any safety, efficacy or manufacturing concern - a procedural clock reset, not a signal about the drug.
recommendations.key_risk: This is a binary, single-asset, lottery-ticket position and is sized at 1% for that reason. A Complete Response Letter on 2026-11-22 takes the stock well below the 4.60 stop in a single gap that no stop can honour. Savara is a pre-revenue small cap trading $7.8M/day: a capital raise ahead of a commercial launch is the most likely way this thesis dies before the FDA ever rules, and the 2026-08-11 S-8 filing is a reminder that share issuance is live. Halt risk around the decision is real. RED TEAM: treat the 3.86:1 as decorative rather than as this trade's ratio. The 8.00 target is reachable only through the 2026-11-22 PDUFA, roughly 48 sessions out and well past the swing horizon this idea is filed under, and the stated plan is to trim into the run-up rather than hold through the decision - so the plan does not actually pursue the target the ratio is computed against.
recommendations.counter_argument: A major amendment means the FDA asked questions substantial enough to need three more months, and companies always frame that as procedural. The stock has gone nowhere for a month - 5.21 to 5.63 since mid-August on falling volume - which is not what a market confident of approval looks like ten weeks out.

evidence.detail: PDUFA target action date 2026-11-22, extended by three months from 2026-08-22, under Priority Review. Confirmed from Savara own announcement text rather than a recalled date.

RED TEAM: this is the same Savara announcement as the dated_catalyst item above, read on stocktitan rather than on the company IR page - one document under two kinds, not two confirmations, which is why conviction came down from 4 to 3. Its content, for the record: the FDA extended the review period by three months because Savara responses to information requests constituted a major amendment to the BLA, and the Agency did not cite any safety, efficacy, or manufacturing concerns in their correspondence. Molgramostim holds Fast Track, Breakthrough Therapy, Orphan Drug (FDA and EMA), MHRA Innovation Passport and Promising Innovative Medicine designations. The release makes no claim about cash runway or launch readiness - an omission worth noting given the dilution risk.

Close 5.30 on 2026-09-11 inside a tight three-week range of 5.21-5.63. ATR14 0.1971 (3.72%), so the 4.60 stop sits 3.55 ATR below the current price - far outside ordinary noise for this name, which is what a binary-event position requires. Avg dollar volume $7.8M/day, comfortably clear of the $500K floor in config/universe.md.

data_quality_notes:
RESEARCH RAN TO COMPLETION. notes.md carries a RESEARCH COMPLETE block at 06:44 ET (superseding one at 06:40), so truncated is false and nothing in this report is reconstructed from fragments. Sixteen candidate lines resolve to fifteen distinct ideas — DINO appears twice and the later line (conviction 5, after the Q2 8-K was read directly) is the one taken. Every idea here was captured by the research phase; none was authored at synthesis.

SHAPE: 15 ideas = 5 genuinely new (DINO, PFE, XLE, CEG, /MBTV6) + 10 updates to the 12 open positions. All 12 open positions have a decision. That ratio is unusual and it is the honest output of a full book going into the week's largest scheduled event: five positions needed closing (LULU, NKE, GLD, BCC, LCII), four are hold-do-not-add (CCJ, SPY, DVN, plus TLT as a reaffirmed avoid), and only SVRA is a hold whose entry zone stays open. Direction skew is deliberately defensive — 5 closes, 2 shorts, 1 avoid against 5 longs — which is what a Fed hiking into a supply shock deserves.
